newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Tech boasts robust 96 result, says more to come.
newsitem.headline: VA Tech boasts robust 96 result, says more to come.

text.p: Austrian engineering firm VA Technologie reported on Wednesday double-digit earnings growth in all key areas apart from net profit in 1996 and said it proposed raising its dividend by two schillings.
For the current year, VA Tech said it would continue on its adopted growth course and would turn in another quality set of earnings.
"VA Tech will further grow in business volume and earnings, paying high attention to globalisation, technological development and group integration," it said, without giving further details.

VA Tech said 1996 group pretax profit jumped 32 percent to 1.672 billion schillings ($137.6 million), sales climbed 29 percent to 33.537 billion and order intake rose 26 percent to 44.576 billion, while net profit gained just five percent to 1.404 billion.

"Net profit was influenced by a temporarily higher company taxation (due to the suspended use of tax loss carry forwards for 1996 and 1997) as well as by the absence of extraordinary income in 1996," VA Tech said in a statement.

Order backlog, however, again reached a new record at 80.4 billion schillings , up 21 percent from 1995. The company attributed this to its risk management, whereby it spreads the sizes of projects so that the group is not dependent on a few major projects.

Indeed, middle-sized projects with a value from 100 million to one billion schillings accounted for approximately 50 percent of the order backlog value, while only 26 percent came from major projects with a value of more than one billion schillings.
The group's order intake, which rose 26 percent, was boosted by the acquisition of Germany's Fuchs Systemtechnik and by the environmental engineering area of Sulzer Chemtech, VA Tech said.
Order intake by division showed a 34 percent increase for metallurgical engineering, 35 percent rise for energy and environmental engineering, and 31 percent jump for plant engineering and services.

VA Tech continued its globalisation drive last year. In addition to acquisitions in Germany, Switzerland and Croatia, new international units were established in Brazil and Great Britain as well as joint ventures in Saudi Arabia and India.
VA Tech now has 200 units worldwide. ($ = 12.15 Austrian Schillings)
